newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bewag expects greater productivity after sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Bewag expects greater productivity after sell-off.

text.p: The predominantly state-held German utility Berlin Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag) said on Monday it expects its productivity to increase after its planned privatisation has been completed.

Speaking at Bewag's annual shareholder meeting, chief executive Dietmar Winje said that the group wants to expand its areas of operation after its planned sell-off by the city-state of Berlin, which Winje said should be viewed as an opportunity.
Winje told shareholders that after the sale of Berlin's shareholding, the company expects any future investors to strengthen the company economically and improve its competitiveness.

Electricity turnover in the first three months of the business year was 724 million marks, Winje said. In the year to the end of June 1995/96, Bewag reported net profits of 169 million marks, with a dividend of eight marks per share.
Currently 50.8 percent of the Bewag company is owned by Berlin, with 10 percent held by Viag AG unit Bayernwerk and Veba AG's PreussenElektra, respectively.
The remaining shares are spread among smaller shareholders.
